title: Autoscaler deadband rebalancing retrospective and warm-provisioner action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Retrospective for a production capacity regression caused by aggressive autoscaler deadband and probe sensitivity changes. This ticket captures root cause analysis, immediate mitigations we applied during the incident, and a prioritized action plan to avoid recurrence by combining deadband rebalancing, warm-provisioner improvements, and more robust signal aggregation for HPA/KEDA.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-18 between 03:12-03:42 UTC we observed a large number of 5xx and increased tail latencies in the hosted inference cluster serving small-chat workloads. The cluster underprovisioned during a burst because the autoscaler did not react quickly to an increase in p95/p99 latency and KEDA triggers were suppressed by a recent deadband tuning change. Cold-start amplification from scale events caused request queuing and cascading further scale decisions.
impact_summary: ~12% request error rate for impacted routes, median latency increased from 85ms to 420ms, peak p99s exceeded SLOs by ~2.5x. Two mid-size customers saw degraded SLAs and one Support ticket escalated to Priority 1. No data loss reported. Total incident duration until stable capacity restored: ~30 minutes.
timeline: 2026-02-18 03:12 UTC: First spike in p95/p99 observed by alerting (p95 > 250ms)
2026-02-18 03:15 UTC: Autoscaler logs show suppressed scale due to deadband policy change deployed 2026-02-16
2026-02-18 03:18 UTC: KEDA trigger telemetry reports large short-lived event bursts but trigger smoothing kept rate below threshold
2026-02-18 03:22 UTC: On-call enabled emergency warm-provisioner (manual warm pool fill) and increased KEDA sensitivity for affected clusters
2026-02-18 03:28 UTC: Instances started to register healthy and request queuing decreased; error rate falls back to baseline by 03:42 UTC
root_cause: A combination of (1) a recently tightened autoscaler deadband configuration intended to reduce scale churn, (2) KEDA smoothing configuration that averaged out short high-amplitude bursts, and (3) no warm-provisioner priming for this specific traffic cohort. The deadband change was applied globally without per-cohort calibration, so small-chat workloads with bursty tail-latency patterns were underrecognized by the controller.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the deadband tightening to previous thresholds (hotfix 2026-02-18), temporarily reduced KEDA smoothing window on affected clusters, and triggered manual warm-pool fill for the Chat-small fleet. Pager duty runbook used to expedite manual actions.
permanent_mitigation: Plan includes implementing cohort-aware deadband (per-route/prefix), introducing an adaptive deadband that uses tail-latency percentiles rather than mean rates, integrating warm-provisioner pre-warming for high-tail cohorts, and enhancing HPA/KEDA aggregation metric to expose p95/p99 latency instead of avg. We will also add a safety path that triggers fallback to a higher-capacity model variant when observed queuing increases beyond threshold.
action_items: ENG-AP-1: Implement cohort-aware deadband config keyed by route tags (team: runtime). Estimate 5 pts. Due 2026-03-17.
ENG-AP-2: Add p95/p99 latency as first-class metric for HPA and KEDA scaling decisions and surface in autoscaler API (team: metrics). Estimate 3 pts. Due 2026-03-24.

ENG-AP-3: Extend warm-provisioner to support targeted priming by cohort with synthetic micro-requests to populate KV cache. Include backoff to avoid overprovisioning (team: infra). Estimate 5 pts. Due 2026-04-07.

ENG-AP-4: Create an experiment to run dynamic deadband annealing (three-stage: conservative->normal->aggressive) behind a feature flag and measure scale churn vs. tail-latency impact. Rollout to 10% of clusters first. (team: runtime/experiments). Estimate 8 pts. Due 2026-04-14.
ENG-AP-5: Add dashboard and alert: 'p99-driven underprovisioning' that correlates queue depth, p99, and KEDA suppression count. (team: observability). Estimate 2 pts. Due 2026-03-10.
ENG-AP-6: Author runbook updates for rapid warm-provisioner invocation and deadband rollback steps; include contact matrix for dedicated customers. (team: SRE). Estimate 1 pt. Due 2026-03-05.
follow_up_tasks: Run A/B with feature-flagged deadband on two non-production clusters for 2 weeks and collect scale-churn and latency tradeoffs.
Validate warm-provisioner synthetic priming does not negatively affect model cache eviction policies by running 48h soak tests.
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to notify top-10 affected customers about changes and expected mitigation timelines.
Add integration tests that simulate short high-amplitude bursts and assert correct scaling behavior without oscillation.
decisions: Decision: Use tail-latency (p95/p99) as the primary scaling signal for conversational cohorts where QoE is sensitive to bursts.
Decision: Keep global default deadband conservative but allow per-cohort overrides via config map to avoid cascading regressions.
Decision: Warm-provisioner will default to targeted priming for cohorts meeting burstiness threshold; manual override available in Console.
tradeoffs: Tighter deadband reduces cost and unnecessary churn but risks underprovisioning for bursty workloads. Warm-provisioner increases cost slightly for primed capacity but reduces customer-impacting latency spikes. p99-driven scaling is more noisy; we mitigate by combining with cohort-aware hysteresis and annealing windows.
